conviction_note: The evidence points both ways. Toast's own beat pattern (Q2 recurring gross profit $595M against a $565-575M guide, adjusted EBITDA $211M ex-refund against $185-195M) and a soft consensus for location adds lean toward a beat. Against that sit the CFO's statement that the memory-cost P&L hit will be larger in 2027 than in 2026, an FTC/eight-state lawsuit filed 2026-10-29, a +6.5% five-day run-up (+5.5% on Monday on light pre-earnings buying) and +22 vol points of put skew. So p_up is 48 on an abs_move of 10, close to the 10.87% event-implied move. The findings sum to -0.5 and the scaled number is -0.4; they agree.
bar: Company Q3 guide: non-GAAP subscription+fintech gross profit $615-625M (22-24% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $210-220M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650164/000165016426000162/tost-20260630xexhibit991.htm, 2026-08-04). Two agreeing estimate sources for revenue: Zacks $1.96B revenue, $0.37 EPS, GPV $61.94B, locations 187,891, total ARR $2.50B (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/insights-toast-tost-q3-wall-131502381.html, 2026-11-02); Investing.com $1.97B revenue, $0.37 EPS (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/toast-set-to-report-earnings-as-software-upsell-strategy-faces-test-93CH-4996020, 2026-11-03). Other aggregators show $0.25-0.26 EPS ($2.01B revenue on Chartmill/FXEmpire), probably a GAAP-vs-adjusted difference. Street recurring-gross-profit consensus is unsourced, so the guide is the bar for that line. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 34.27M shares, 3.7 days to cover, as of the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/tost). It was 34.3M / 3.6 days on 2026-08-19 and 44.2M on 2026-06-30, so it is falling and not crowded (roughly 6-8% of float; Benzinga's undated page says 8.3%). Borrow fee about 0.4% (curvedtrading.com). The baseline has 25-delta skew at +22.36 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI ratio 1.26, ATM IV 135% on the 11-06 expiry, and an event-implied move of 10.87%. Run-up: +6.47% over 5 days and +11.82% over 20 days into the print, 13% below the 52-week high. Monday 2026-11-02 closed +5.5% ($31.68 to $33.42) on what Benzinga called pre-earnings buying.

findings.finding: Toast has beaten its own guide top by a wide margin and the Q3 guide steps growth down: Q2 recurring gross profit was $595M (+28%) against a $565-575M guide (+3.5% over the top), and adjusted EBITDA was $221M including a ~$10M tariff refund ($211M ex-refund) against $185-195M (+8%). The Q3 guide of $615-625M implies only 22-24% growth, against the 27-28% delivered in Q1 and Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Toast has not reliably paid for beats. The Q2 2026 beat-and-raise traded +2.93%. The Q1 2026 beat was sold -14.74% because the Q2 EBITDA guide came in below the Street. Q4 2025 +4.55%, Q3 2025 +9.48%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. A guide-top beat is Toast's known habit, and Monday's +5.5% on light volume was explicitly pre-earnings buying. If the market had fully priced a ~3% recurring-gross-profit beat, the 25-delta skew would not be +22 points toward puts. The open question is the size of the beat relative to a whisper.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release shows the same pattern: Q1 recurring gross profit $529M (+27%), Q2 guide $565-575M implying 22-24% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650164/000165016426000113/tost-20260331xexhibit991.htm). Same company, a different document.

findings.finding: The Street's implied location adds look undemanding. Zacks consensus is 187,891 locations against ~180,000 at June 30, implying ~7,900 net adds in Q3, against a record ~9,500 in Q2 that management said came mostly from core SMB/mid-market with win rates 'strong'. Consensus GPV of $61.94B is only +2% q/q from $60.7B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 record net adds (9,500) came with a +2.93% reaction. The Q3 2025 print, where ARR was a 'notable miss' but adds and profit beat, traded +9.48% per a 2025 recap.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus location count is a derived Zacks number, not a headline expectation. Previews (Investing.com 11-03) frame the debate around revenue per location and DashOS, not adds. If buy-side expectations for adds were already near 9,000+, a sell-side model at 187.9k would have been revised up, and Zacks shows revenue estimates 'largely unchanged' over 60 days.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript: record 9,500 adds, strong win rates (https://www.webull.com/news/15386954068485120). BofA's 2027 net-add forecast is ~10% above the Street (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/toast-set-to-report-earnings-as-software-upsell-strategy-faces-test-93CH-4996020).

findings.finding: Fiserv, which reported 2026-11-03 before the open (after Toast last spoke), had Merchant Solutions organic revenue down 2% and gave no Clover revenue or GPV number, only 'consistent underlying growth'. Chipotle's Q3 comps were +2.1% (traffic +0.8%) after a July dip that recovered by end-August. Read together: no restaurant-spend collapse in Q3, and the largest SMB-POS rival is still soft, which supports Toast's share gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on peer read-through. Q2 2026's strong same-store-sales commentary came with +2.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Fiserv release came out the same morning, and a Clover read is hard to quantify without a Clover number. This is a proxy and partly priced. If the market read Fiserv as a Toast share-gain signal, TOST would have outperformed today; it is +0.2% intraday (33.89 vs 33.82 sealed).
findings.independence: Chipotle 8-K Q3 2026: comps +2.1%, July low-single-digit headwind recovered by end of August (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001058090/000105809026000103/cmg-20261028xex991.htm). A different company and document; both are proxies.

findings.finding: The buyback authorization is nearly used up. Toast bought $486M year to date through June 30 ($163M in Q2), leaving only ~$100M under the program at June 30. At the Q2 pace it was likely exhausted in Q3, so a new authorization with this print is plausible. The last increase ($500M) was announced with the Q4 2025 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The February 2026 $500M increase came with the Q4 2025 print, which traded +4.55%. The aggregator story 'Toast jumps as fresh 10-K highlights expanded $500M buyback authorization' suggests the market rewarded it.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview mentions the authorization running out. Inference, not a company statement: management only said it will buy 'opportunistically'. If the Street expected a new program, previews would list it as a catalyst.
findings.independence: Q2 call: ~$100M remaining, opportunistic buybacks (https://www.webull.com/news/15386954068485120). This is the same fact from a second document, so it counts once.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-10, after Toast's Q2 call, Adyen announced it is expanding its Toast partnership into the US, Toast's largest market (215B trailing GPV). Toast says Adyen joins its existing US processing partners. That is a processing-cost lever under the payments take rate, which management already credited for a y/y increase ('cost optimization').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's take-rate improvement (payments 50bp) came with a +2.93% reaction. No specific history on processor changes.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and was covered in trade press. Rollout timing and economics are undisclosed, and a cost benefit would show only in the fintech gross margin or the 2027 framing. Mostly priced; small.
findings.independence: Trade coverage says Adyen sits beneath Toast Payments, with lower restaurant costs not guaranteed (https://merchantcostconsulting.com/lower-credit-card-processing-fees/toast-us-adyen-deal-restaurant-processing-rates/). Related, not independent confirmation.

findings.finding: Memory costs are a forward-guide risk. On the Q2 call the CFO said 'I would expect the P&L impact in '27 to be greater than '26 just based on how we account for inventory'. The hardware gross loss widened to $68M from $54M y/y, inventories nearly doubled to $217M, and there are $194M of non-cancellable hardware purchase commitments. TrendForce reportedly raised its PC DRAM contract forecasts to +15-20% q/q for Q3 2026 and +3-8% for Q4. Any first 2027 framing, or an implied Q4 EBITDA below the Street, lands on the line that produced the -14.74% reaction in May.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026: a Q1 beat was overshadowed by a Q2 EBITDA guide below the Street and memory-cost commentary, and the stock fell -14.74%. February 2026's higher-hardware-cost outlook also weighed for weeks, but that print still traded +4.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The put skew (+22) is consistent with guide risk. Q4 implied EBITDA from the FY guide (805-825 minus H1 400 minus Q3 210-220) is ~$175-205M, below Q3, and previews do not discuss it. Toast normally gives the formal 2027 guide in February, so the November call is where qualitative 2027 margin commentary first appears.
findings.independence: TrendForce DRAM forecast raise via a KuCoin/ChainThink snippet (https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/trendforce-raises-q3-q4-dram-contract-price-forecasts-benefits-micron). Its date is unverified and it is an industry proxy. The Q2 10-Q's $194M hardware purchase obligations come from a separate primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650164/000165016426000164/tost-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: The FTC plus eight states (CA, CO, FL, IL, IA, NE, OK, UT) sued Toast on 2026-10-29 in N.D. Cal. under the FTC Act and ROSCA. They allege hidden fees in the $0 'Pay-as-you-Go' plan (cost recovered through higher processing fees), unauthorized add-ons, hard cancellation with early termination fees, an undisclosed 99-cent diner fee (2021-2023, not refunded) and false 24/7 support claims. They seek injunctive relief, compensation and civil penalties. The Q2 10-Q disclosed a June 2026 draft complaint and proposed settlement, with no accrual and no estimable loss. The call will be the first time management is questioned on it, including any change to pricing or contract terms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The filing day, 2026-10-29, closed -1.4% ($31.94 to $31.50) on 12.9M shares, 1.7x the 20-day average. The stock then rose +0.6% and +5.5% over the next two sessions, so the market has so far looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: The suit itself is priced (a -1.4% day, then fully recovered). What is not priced is any Q3 accrual, which the 10-Q said was not estimable in August, and any change to the $0 plan's processing premium or termination fees, which would hit the fintech take rate. The rebound past the pre-suit price says the market assumes neither.
findings.independence: FTC press release (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-states-take-action-against-toast-inc-over-hidden-unauthorized-fees-deceptive-subscription). Q2 10-Q Note 11: June 2026 draft complaint, no estimable loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650164/000165016426000164/tost-20260630.htm). San Francisco City Attorney suit as well (https://www.sf.gov/news-city-attorney-chiu-sues-toast-for-trapping-restaurants-in-subscriptions-riddled-with-unauthorized-fees).

findings.finding: The stock has run up into the print. It is +6.47% over 5 days and +11.82% over 20 days, and Monday 2026-11-02 rose +5.5% on what Benzinga called pre-earnings buying, with no company news. Against that, the 25-delta skew is +22.36 vol points toward puts and the put/call OI ratio is 1.26. The bar for a positive reaction is now higher than it was for the Q2 print, which traded +2.93% from a lower base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print came after a ~52% three-month rally and traded only +2.93%. The stock then drifted from $35.32 (08-20) to ~$29-30 by early October.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the run-up has used up some of the beat. Not crowded: short interest is 3.7 days to cover and falling, so there is little squeeze fuel to offset it.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's run-up and skew, plus Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TOST?range=1mo&interval=1d).

Jefferies sees it pressuring Toast's add-on software (IQ Grow, marketing/analytics) rather than core POS, and previews frame it as the test for the software-upsell thesis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print reacted to this line. The stock fell -3.4% on 10-14 and rose +7.9% on 10-15 (the BofA re-initiation at Buy, $40).
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Jefferies note, month per DashOS coverage dated 2026-10-01)
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and debated (Truist calls it overblown). It matters only if management's subscription-ARPU commentary disappoints. Small.
findings.independence: Technobezz on the DashOS launch partner list (https://www.technobezz.com/news/doordash-launches-dashos-restaurant-platform). Investing.com preview on DashOS concerns (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/toast-set-to-report-earnings-as-software-upsell-strategy-faces-test-93CH-4996020).

findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4s three months old, largely planned or trust sales. Close to zero information, filed for completeness.

baseline_tension: The negative findings (memory guide, FTC, run-up) agree with the +22 put skew and are probably partly priced. The positive findings (habitual guide-top beat, soft implied adds) cut against the skew, but Monday's +5.5% pre-earnings rally has already taken part of them. Net, the evidence does not beat the baseline, so p_up sits at 48.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding went from +0.8 to +0.5, because Q2's beat-and-raise bought only +2.93% and Q1's beat was sold -14.74%.

Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): the Fiserv/Chipotle peer read went from +0.3 to +0.2 and the Adyen processing-cost lever from +0.2 to +0.1. Net adds trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 because the consensus location count is a derived Zacks number.

Lesson 7 (skew is the thing to beat): the negatives on memory (-0.8 to -0.7) and FTC (-0.6 to -0.5) agree with the +22 put skew, and the FTC day was already absorbed (-1.4%, then fully recovered), so both were shrunk as partly priced. Short interest was checked: 3.7 days to cover and falling, not crowded.
Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue bar has two agreeing sources (Zacks $1.96B, Investing $1.97B). The recurring-gross-profit bar is only the company guide, so the reported-quarter findings stay small.
Scaled measurement: abs_move raised from 9 to 10, nearer the 10.87% implied move, per the core's note that hunters understate. p_up moved from 49 to 48.
